assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Closed system
items.clue: Apparatus from which no reactants or products can escape.

items.label: Tangent
items.clue: A straight line drawn so that it just touches a curve at one point.

items.label: Reversible reaction
items.clue: The products can themselves combine to re-form the starting substances.

items.label: Equilibrium
items.clue: Reached when the forward and backward changes happen at exactly the same rate.

questions.stem: Required practical 5 investigates how changes in concentration affect the rate of reaction. Which pair of methods does the specification require?

options.text: Measuring the volume of a gas, and following the temperature rise in the flask
Measuring the volume of a gas, and following a colour change or turbidity
Measuring the temperature rise, and following a colour change or turbidity
Weighing the solid left behind, and following the volume of the solution used

questions.explanation: These are the two methods named in Required practical 5.

questions.stem: Why does increasing the concentration of hydrochloric acid increase the rate of its reaction with magnesium?

options.text: The acid particles move faster, so their collisions carry more energy
The activation energy of the reaction is lowered by the extra acid
More particles in the same volume means more frequent collisions
Each single collision becomes much more likely to end in a reaction

questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of reactants in solution increases the frequency of collisions.

questions.stem: On a reaction profile for a catalysed reaction, how does the catalysed curve differ from the uncatalysed one?

options.text: Its hump is lower, and the reactants and products are unchanged
Its hump is lower, and the products end up at a lower energy too
Its hump is lower, and it makes more product as well
The hump is the same, but the curve reaches products sooner

questions.explanation: The lower hump shows the lower activation energy of the new pathway; the energy levels stay the same.

questions.stem: A sample of blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate is heated and turns white. What must be done to turn it blue again?

options.text: Nothing will work, as the direction is fixed once heating has started
Heat the white solid much more strongly for a longer period of time
Add water to the white solid, changing the conditions back again
Grind the white solid to a powder to raise its surface area

questions.explanation: The direction of reversible reactions can be changed by changing the conditions; adding water reverses the change that heating produced.

questions.stem: Required practical 5 should involve developing a hypothesis. Which of these is a suitable hypothesis for the investigation?

options.text: The higher the concentration of the acid, the faster gas will be produced
Measure the volume of gas every ten seconds for each concentration used
Add the acid to the magnesium and time each reaction with a stopwatch
Concentration and rate of reaction are connected in some way

questions.explanation: It is a testable prediction linking the independent variable to the dependent variable.

questions.stem: A 5 g strip of magnesium and 5 g of magnesium powder are added to separate beakers of the same acid. Why does the powder react faster?

options.text: There is simply more magnesium in the powder than in the strip
It has a larger surface area to volume ratio, so collisions are more frequent
The powder particles move faster, so the collisions are more energetic
The powder must lower the activation energy needed by the reaction

questions.explanation: The effect of the size of the pieces is explained in terms of surface area to volume ratio.

questions.stem: The equation for a reaction is 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. A solid is added to the flask, the reaction speeds up, and the solid is recovered unchanged at the end. What is the solid?

options.text: A reactant, because it was added to the flask before the reaction started
A catalyst, as it speeds the reaction up and is not in the equation
A product, because it was there in the flask at the end of the reaction
An enzyme, because it is a solid substance that speeds the reaction up

questions.explanation: Catalysts are identified from their effect on the rate and from their absence from the chemical equation.

questions.stem: Ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride is given as an example of a reversible reaction. White ammonium chloride is heated in a tube and the two gases form. Which statement about this example is correct?

options.text: The ammonium chloride has been destroyed for good
Half of the solid always stays behind unchanged
The two gases must react first, before the solid heats
Cooling the gases re-forms ammonium chloride

questions.stem: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of a reaction? Give the full reason.

options.text: Collisions are more frequent, and that is the whole of the reason why
Collisions happen more often, and nothing else about them changes
The activation energy of the reaction falls as it is heated
Collisions are more frequent and more of them are energetic enough

questions.explanation: Increasing the temperature increases the frequency of collisions and makes the collisions more energetic.

questions.stem: Two gases react together. Why does increasing the pressure of the gases increase the rate of reaction?

options.text: Squeezing the particles closer together makes each collision harder
Raising the pressure lowers the energy that a successful collision needs
There are more gas particles present than there were before
The particles are in a smaller volume, so they collide more often

questions.explanation: Increasing the pressure of reacting gases increases the frequency of collisions.

questions.stem: Doubling the concentration of a solution roughly doubles the rate of reaction. Using simple ideas about proportionality, what should halving the concentration do?

options.text: Cut the rate to a quarter, since the rate depends on the square
Cut the rate by more than half, as the particles also move slower
Leave the rate unchanged, since the same amount of acid still reacts
Roughly halve the rate, as collisions become half as frequent

questions.explanation: Simple proportionality: half the particles in the same volume gives about half the collision frequency.

questions.stem: What can Le Chatelier's Principle be used for?

options.text: Predicting the effect of changing conditions on a system at equilibrium
Calculating the exact amount of each product present at the new equilibrium
Predicting how long a given mixture will take to reach equilibrium again
Showing that heating a reaction always increases its yield

questions.explanation: The effects of changing conditions on a system at equilibrium can be predicted using Le Chatelier's Principle.

questions.stem: In the equilibrium 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3, sulfur trioxide (SO3) is continuously removed from the mixture. What happens?

options.text: More reactants form, because there is now less product present
More reactants react until equilibrium is reached again
Nothing happens, because the system stays at equilibrium
The mixture ends up holding equal amounts of each one

questions.explanation: If the concentration of a product is decreased, more reactants will react until equilibrium is reached again.

questions.stem: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is increased. What happens to the relative amount of products?

options.text: It increases, because the forward reaction is the exothermic one
It decreases, because the forward reaction gives out energy
It increases, since heating always improves any yield
It stays the same, since heating changes only the rates

questions.explanation: The relative amount of products at equilibrium decreases for an exothermic reaction when the temperature is increased.

questions.stem: For the gaseous equilibrium 2SO3(g) ⇌ 2SO2(g) + O2(g), the pressure is decreased. Which way does the equilibrium position shift?

options.text: To the left, towards the side with just two gas molecules
Neither way, since the numbers of atoms are equal here
Neither way, as pressure changes only alter rates
To the right, the side with three molecules of gas

questions.explanation: A decrease in pressure shifts the position towards the side with the larger number of molecules: two on the left, three on the right.

questions.stem: In a sealed flask N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g). The forward reaction is exothermic. More nitrogen is pumped into the flask at constant temperature. What is the qualitative prediction?

options.text: Less ammonia is present at the new equilibrium
More ammonia forms at the new equilibrium
The amount of ammonia present cannot change
Ammonia forms faster but its amount is fixed

questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant means more products are formed until equilibrium is reached again.

questions.stem: A sealed flask holds an equilibrium mixture of hydrogen, iodine and hydrogen iodide: H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI. Extra hydrogen is injected and the flask is left until equilibrium is reached again. What is found?

options.text: Less HI, and more iodine than there was before
The same HI and the same iodine as before
More HI, and less iodine than there was
Only the hydrogen is now at a higher level than before

questions.explanation: Increasing a reactant concentration forms more product, and forming more HI uses up some of the iodine.
